questions.question: Discuss the following - swivel weave, lappet weave, spot weave.
questions.solution_html:
• Swivel Weave: Swivel weave is produced by the use of extra filling yarns. The yarns used
  • in each pattern are wound on quills and placed in shuttles, which are placed at each point
  • where the design is to appear. This particular weaving process permits
  • weaving in different colours in the same row, because each design has its own shuttle.
  • The design created is the same on both the front and the back side. The fabric has small
  • geometrical patterns and used for apparel and furnishings.
  • Lappet Weave: Lappet weave introduces one continuous additional yarn in a way that it
  • creates designs over predetermined portions of the basic fabric. One continuous additional
  • yarn is carried on the back of the fabric from one design to the next. The floating thread is cut
  • and the ends are secured. These fabrics are superior to fabrics made with a swivel weave.
  • Spot Weave: Spot weave is manufactured by the use of either extra warp or filling yarns. The
  • yarns are inserted in the entire length or width of the fabric in predetermined areas and the
  • pattern is formed using either dobby or jacquard attachments. When not in use, the extra yarns
  • float across the back of the fabric. This makes the Uncut spot pattern or Unclipped. At times
  • when small and widely spaced patterns are made, the floating yarns are out from the back side
  • of the fabric and this is known as the Cut spot yarns or clipped.
questions.final_answer: of the fabric and this is known as the Cut spot yarns or clipped

questions.question: Explain the physical, chemical and microscopic test of silk. END OF THE QUESTION PAPER ***
questions.solution_html:
• Physical properties of silk
  • a) Fine smooth and even fabric. It is white in color with very high luster.
  • b) Medium weight fiber.
  • c) Thinnest natural fiber and very strong.
  • d) Retain its shape and resist wrinkles due to its elastic properties.
  • e) Excellent drapability.
  • f) Absorbs moisture readily.
  • g) It is a non-conductor of heat and therefore desirable for winter wear
  • Microscopic test
  •  L.S: Under the microscope the silk fiber looks like a smooth glass rod.
  •  C.S: Smooth triangular cross section
  • Chemical properties
  •  Alkaline solutions cause the silk filament to swell.
  •  Silk is degraded more readily by acids; Concentrated sulfuric and hydrochloric acids
  • especially when hot, dissolves silk.
  • Prepared by
  • Ms. Sruthy Mohan
  • Assistant Professor
  • Department of Fashion Design
  • Yeldo Mar Baselios College
  • Kothamangalam
questions.final_answer: Option Fine smooth and even fabric. It is white in color with very high luster.

questions.question: Discuss the following - swivel weave, lappet weave, spot weave.
questions.solution_html:
• Swivel Weave: Swivel weave is produced by the use of extra filling yarns. The yarns used
  • in each pattern are wound on quills and placed in shuttles, which are placed at each point
  • where the design is to appear. This particular weaving process permits
  • weaving in different colours in the same row, because each design has its own shuttle.
  • The design created is the same on both the front and the back side. The fabric has small
  • geometrical patterns and used for apparel and furnishings.
  • Lappet Weave: Lappet weave introduces one continuous additional yarn in a way that it
  • creates designs over predetermined portions of the basic fabric. One continuous additional
  • yarn is carried on the back of the fabric from one design to the next. The floating thread is cut
  • and the ends are secured. These fabrics are superior to fabrics made with a swivel weave.
  • Spot Weave: Spot weave is manufactured by the use of either extra warp or filling yarns. The
  • yarns are inserted in the entire length or width of the fabric in predetermined areas and the
  • pattern is formed using either dobby or jacquard attachments. When not in use, the extra yarns
  • float across the back of the fabric. This makes the Uncut spot pattern or Unclipped. At times
  • when small and widely spaced patterns are made, the floating yarns are out from the back side
  • of the fabric and this is known as the Cut spot yarns or clipped.
questions.final_answer: of the fabric and this is known as the Cut spot yarns or clipped

questions.question: Differentiate between Blends and Mixtures. / Part E Long Answer Questions
questions.solution_html:
• Blending is the process of combining two or more different types of
  • fibres -Quality not considered. Same properties of fibres are used for blending.
  • A blend occurs when two or more different fibers are spun together into a single
  • yarn before weaving or knitting. The fibers are mixed at the fiber stage, creating
  • a yarn where the fibers are intimately combined.
  • Mixtures – same fibers of different properties- quality is considered.
  • Different properties of fibres are used for mixing. A mixture refers to the use of
  • different types of yarns made from different fibers in the warp and weft
  • directions of woven fabrics or in different sections of knitted fabrics. Unlike
  • blends, fibers in mixtures remain separate and are combined at the fabric
  • construction stage.
  • Long Answer Questions

questions.question: Explain the essential properties required for a successful textile fibre?
questions.solution_html:
• Strength (Tenacity)- The fiber must have sufficient tensile strength to
  • withstand the stresses of spinning, weaving, and general wear and tear.
  • flexibility- A fiber must be able to bend without breaking to be manipulated and
  • twisted around other fibers during yarn formation.
  • Uniformity- For consistent quality, fibers should have uniformity in length
  • diameter, and other properties.
  • Fibre length to width ratio- Fibers need to be significantly longer than they
  • are wide to be spun into strong, smooth yarns.\
  • Cohesiveness or spinning quality- This is the ability of fibers to cling to one
  • another, which is crucial for spinning
questions.final_answer: another, which is crucial for spinning
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write in detail on properties of viscose rayon.
questions.solution_html:
• Strength - Viscose has moderate dry strength, but it loses 40-70% of its
  • strength when wet. Elasticity- Lacks elasticity; it has poor resilience.
  • Drapability- Exhibits excellent drapability, which makes it suitable for flowing
  • garments.
  • Heat adsorbent- Rayon begins to decompose at high temperatures (~150–
  • 200°C).Scorches easily and should be ironed at low temperatures.
  • Washability- Requires gentle handling during washing.
  • Shrinkage- Viscose rayon has a high tendency to shrink, especially when it
  • becomes wet.
  • Reaction to acids and alkalis- Weak acids: fairly resistant. Strong acids: cause
  • hydrolysis and weaken fiber. Alkalis: Strong alkalis (like caustic soda) damage
  • viscose rayon; mild alkalis cause swelling.
  • Mildew- Viscose rayon is highly prone to mildew and fungal attack.
  • Dyeability- Viscose rayon has very high dyeability due to Its high moisture
  • regain.
  • .
questions.final_answer: Option (c) .Scorches easily and should be ironed at low temperatures.
